NOTICE OF IMPENDING POWER TO SELL TAX DEFAULTED PROPERTY 

Pursuant to Section 3361-3362 pf the California Revenue and Taxation Code 

And shall be published annually, on or before June 8 

I certify, under the penalty of perjury, the foregoing is true and correct. 

/S/ Shari L. Freidenrich, CPA, CCMT, CPFA, CPFIM, ACPFIM 

Orange County Treasurer-Tax Collector 

Executed at Orange County, Santa Ana, California on May 26, 2026. 

Published in the Orange County Business Journal on June 1, June 8 and June 15, 2026. 

Notice is hereby given that the real properties described below will, by operation of law, become subject to the Tax Collector’s power to sell that occurs when five or more years have lapsed from the date that at least one installment of the property taxes became delinquent and unpaid and are considered tax defaulted. 

The parcels listed herein will become subject to the Tax Collector’s power to sell on July 1, 2026, at 12:01 a.m., by operation of law, for non-payment of taxes and will be sold unless redemption (payment in full) of all unpaid property taxes, assessments, penalties and fees as prescribed by law is made by June 30, 2026, or

a Five-Year Installment Plan for eligible properties is established prior to 5 p.m. on June 30, 2026. After July 1, 2026, a Five-Year Installment Plan will no longer be available for any properties listed herein, and the entire balance due, that includes any penalties and interest, must be paid in full to prevent the sale of the

property at public auction. The right of redemption (payment in full) will terminate at 5 p.m. on the last business day prior to the date of the auction. 

All information concerning redemption of tax-defaulted property will be furnished, upon request by Shari L. Freidenrich, Treasurer-Tax Collector, by email at AskTaxCollector@octreasurer.gov, in person at the County Service Center at 601 North Ross St., Santa Ana, by going to the Frequently Asked Questions and

selecting Delinquent Secured Property at octreasurer.gov/faq or by calling (714)834-3411. This notice will be posted online at octreasurer.gov/PublishedNotices and filed with the Clerk Recorder. 

The amounts necessary to redeem (pay in full) the tax-defaulted properties are set forth opposite the parcel numbers as of June 30, 2026. These amounts include all defaulted property taxes, penalties and costs that have been accrued since the date of delinquency through June 30, 2026. To obtain the balance due after

June 30, 2026, scan the QR code below and enter the Assessor’s Parcel Number (APN) or physical address at TaxBill.octreasurer.gov,   email AskTaxCollector@octreasurer.gov, or call (714)834-3411 or as the total amount due may include additional penalties and fees as prescribed by law. 

In the event the tax-defaulted parcel identified below is an asset of the estate in a bankruptcy proceeding and subject to the automatic stay provisions set forth at 11 U.S.C. 362, the Tax Collector will not offer the parcel for sale at a tax sale or public auction while the bankruptcy is active, without obtaining an order for

relief from the automatic stay. 

Parcel Numbering System Explanation 

The APN, when used to describe property in this list, refers to the assessor’s map book, the map page, the block on the map (if applicable), and the individual parcel on the map page or in the block. The assessor’s maps and further explanation of the parcel numbering system are available from the Office of the Assessor.
